Alright, the fetcher script I just launched is running asynchronously in the background. I need to monitor its progress before I proceed to build the rest of the game engine. The script is supposed to download all Gen‑1 Pokémon data and the FireRed/LeafGreen sprites, then write out several files under `assets/data` and `assets/sprites`. 

First, I should verify that the background task is actually making progress and not stalled. The task ID is `brh8zidmk`, and its output is being written to a temporary file at `C:\Users\aranr\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\D--project-5\d9c29410-80a6-4e34-aab1-0c7e5bb7110f\tasks\brh8zidmk.output`. By tail‑reading the last few lines of that file I can see any console.log messages or errors the script may have emitted. 

Second, while the fetcher is running I can also check the state of the asset directories that should be populated. The script creates `assets/sprites/front` and `assets/sprites/back` and writes PNG files for each Pokémon ID (1‑151). Counting the files in those directories will tell me whether the sprite download is complete or still in progress. 

Third, the script also writes two JavaScript data files: `assets/data/pokedex.js` and `assets/data/moves.js`. Knowing their file sizes will give me a quick sanity check that they contain a reasonable amount of data (they should be several hundred kilobytes each). If the files are empty or very small, something went wrong.

Putting all of this together, the most efficient single PowerShell command is to:
1. Tail the last 6 lines of the task output file to see recent logs.
2. Count the number of files in the front and back sprite folders.
3. Report the byte length of the two data files.

All of these can be done in one command line using `Get-Content -Tail 6` for the log, `Get-ChildItem … .Count` for the sprite counts, and `Get-Item … .Length` for the file sizes. This will give me a concise snapshot of the fetcher’s status and the asset counts, which I can then use to decide whether to wait longer, troubleshoot, or move on to the next development step.

Thus, I will issue a PowerShell tool call with exactly that composite command.

arguments.description: Check fetcher output and asset counts
